$comment: Invariant ids owned by the P2 task `p2-deps-scaffold`. The list is EMPTY, and that is the correct state. This lane installs dependencies, freezes the inter-stage artefact contract, writes the provenance log and the input resolver, and wires a stage/validator registry behind the CLI. It registers no stage and no validator, so `coursekit build es` exits 2 today by design. Every invariant the content pipeline owns is a property of a produced pack — INV-PACK-13 wants a licence resolved before G0 reads a byte, INV-PACK-15 wants codec, bitrate and bytes on a real bank, INV-PACK-17 wants an attribution string reachable from a rendered credits surface — and there is no pack yet. Claiming one here would mean writing a test that asserts a dict has a key and naming it INV-PACK-13, which is exactly the 'owning test that proves nothing' the plan's rule 4 is written against.
heldWithoutAnInvariantId: The inter-stage artefact contract is frozen by digest: tools/coursekit/tests/test_artifacts.py::test_the_contract_digest_is_frozen hashes all nine JSON Schemas with their stages and filenames, so a schema edit in wave 1 fails the build in the same commit instead of surfacing in wave 2 as a lane whose input no longer parses. Every schema is additionalProperties:false and every record is validated on READ as well as on write, because writing is the only path the module controls and reading is where a hand-edited .jsonl shows up

The exit-2 rule is proved BOTH ways. test_exit_two_is_not_vacuous exits 2 with an empty registry, registers all ten stages and exits 0, then removes one and exits 2 again. Without the middle step a dispatcher that exited 2 unconditionally would pass every other test in the file, and 'coursekit build es' exiting 0 with nothing registered is the most expensive lie this tool can tell: no pack, no output, and it reads as a fast build

The 'no literal outside config/' README rule is executable: tests/test_cli.py walks the package with ast and fails on any public UPPER_CASE module-level name bound to a literal outside coursekit/config/, with a falsifier beside it that plants three violations and three near-misses so the walker cannot pass by walking nothing or by excluding everything

Ten constants that deep/10 states wrongly are encoded in config/base.py with the adversarial-review id at the row and asserted in test_artifacts.py: LanguageTool ja has 735 GRAMMAR rules and no spell checker (R1, the exact inverse of the spec); NLLB v1 carries ODC-By and is oracle-only for a stated reason rather than for a page nobody read (R2); the Tatoeba archive is sentences_CC0.tar.bz2, uppercase (R3), and its per-language CC0 subset eliminates es/de/ja rather than shrinking a pool (R4); Piper has no shippable Japanese voice (R7); JParaCrawl is non-commercial by default and forbidden (R8); hermitdave has 62 directories (R9); `effort` errors on claude-haiku-4-5 (R10); the audio bank is 120 MB across three pipelines, not 35-40 MB across one (R13, R14). A lane that reads the spec instead of the code now gets a failing test rather than a plausible bug

tools/coursekit/tests/fixtures/es-mini/: 200 ORIGINAL es/en pairs written for this repository, 160 CC0-1.0 and 40 CC-BY-4.0 with an attribution owner. Both shapes exist because a uniformly CC0 fixture would let an INV-PACK-17 attribution bug pass every test in the suite, and because the review measured the real Tatoeba CC0 subset for Spanish at 2,266 bytes — attribution is the shipping path. Every derived file is recomputed by the tests in plain Python (ids, dedup hashes, the whole frequency list, every lemma frequency, every decile and band); the spaCy lemma map has its own model-gated test so a lemmatiser bump fails there rather than silently re-partitioning the ledger under eight lanes

The `align` and `tts` dependency groups are deliberately NOT synced by CI (pack-ci.yml runs `uv sync --locked` over [tool.uv] default-groups, and torch + onnxruntime do not fit a 20-minute ubuntu job). CI_SYNCED_GROUPS is asserted against pyproject.toml so the two cannot drift, and a stage needing an absent group exits 3 with the install command rather than degrading — a fallback aligner produces word-bank hints wrong in ways V4 cannot catch, and a fallback voice ships audio that is neither content-addressed nor reproducible

pynacl is pinned to the app's key format rather than assumed compatible: test_pynacl_produces_the_spki_the_app_parses builds a 44-byte ed25519 SPKI from a generated key and matches the 12-byte DER prefix in packages/schema/src/signing.ts, and a second test parses the committed packages/schema/keys/pack-signing.pub the same way. `coursekit sign` and the installer agree on the format before either exists
